blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content:
Chiral perturbation theory ($\chi$PT for short) is regarded nowadays as the effective field theory dual to QCD at very low energies. It describes the dynamics of the pseudo--Goldstone bosons ($\pi,\, K,\,\eta$) in an expansion in powers of external momenta and masses. It incorporates the assumed QCD symmetries such as parity, charge conjugation and, most important, the spontaneous breakdown of chiral symmetry.

blocks.content: The external field method was first introduced by Leutwyler [@Leut], and makes easier the computation of QCD Green functions and form factors. It enforces chiral Ward identities exactly by promoting the global chiral symmetry to a local one. blocks.title: Chiral building blocks
blocks.content: $\chi$PT is based on the spontaneous breakdown of the global $G=SU(n_f)_L\otimes SU(n_f)_R$ flavour symmetry down to its subgroup $SU(n_f)_V$. The dynamical fields $\phi^a=(\pi,K,\eta)$ are assumed to be the (pseudo--)Goldstone bosons associated to this breakdown. blocks.title: The chiral Lagrangian
blocks.content: The number of operators entering in the chiral Lagrangian is of course not restricted by symmetry. So in principle there are an infinite number of them, each one multiplied by an unknown coefficient (this is in agreement with the fact that $\chi$PT is not normalizable *stricto sensu*). So if one has to take them all into account in any calculation, loses all predictive power. At low energies (compared with the chiral scale $\Lambda_\chi\sim4\pi F\sim 1\, \mathrm{GeV}$) pieces with lower powers of momentum and quark masses dominate, and this allows to truncate the number of operators. blocks.content: So far we have restricted ourselves to the even--intrinsic sector. blocks.title: Tensor sources in the Resonance chiral theory and the radiative pion decay
blocks.content: It is well known that if one wishes to extend the energy domain of $\chi$PT resonances must be include as active degrees of freedom. The idea of constructing chiral Lagrangians with resonances fields was pioneered in Ref. [@EGPR], but the inclusion of tensor sources was first considered in Ref. [@CMinprogress]. For a consistent introduction of tensor sources one has to consider spin--one resonances of $J^{PC}=1^{+-}$ quantum numbers, first included in Ref. [@Zauner]. blocks.title: Conclusions
blocks.content:
We have included tensor sources in the $\chi$PT formalism and explicitly constructed the $\mathcal{O}(p^4)$ and $\mathcal{O}(p^6)$ Lagrangians. The challenging part of this construction is to find a complete and non--redundant set of operators. For the reduction of the basis we have followed standard procedures. We have demonstrated that there is no odd--intrinsic--parity sector with tensor sources at the $\mathcal{O}(p^6)$ level.
